decisions.executionNote: Raise right arm and begin turning gripper downward toward basket; left stays home. Small startup increments preserve elbow-up continuity.

Lower a little to surround the rear-right egg, close the right gripper, and pause before checking retention.
Lift the grasped egg clear of the basket, keeping closed, then begin moving toward the holder.
RGB shows all four eggs still in basket. Reopen and realign for a deeper grasp on the rear-right egg.
Refine alignment to the shifted egg, lower jaws around its sides, and close fully before lifting.
Lift vertically with closed jaws to check whether the egg is retained before transport.
No egg retained. Correct forward/back alignment to the egg now displaced toward the basket front, then approach with open jaws.
Use wrist view to center the right-hand egg between the fingers, then close while stationary.
Lift vertically with closed jaws and check that the centered egg rises with the gripper.

Move slightly toward the near-right egg and lower the contact plane, then close without translating.
Relieve contact and shift the open gripper toward the robot; wrist image shows the egg behind the closing region. Reassess before closing.
The egg is now centered at the finger closing region in the wrist view. Close while stationary and make a short retention lift.
Reopen and lower the jaw contact area while shifting toward the robot and slightly right, compensating for the forward-tilted tool offset.
Reduce jaw opening to clear basket rim, make a small centering/downward adjustment, then close fully while stationary.
Lift slowly with jaws closed, checking whether the egg follows rather than remaining in the basket.
Switch to the isolated rear-left egg and restore vertical approach. Use a moderate jaw opening to avoid the basket rim.
Descend vertically over the isolated egg with reduced opening, watching for contact before closing.
Center the isolated egg between the jaws, widen briefly to clear its sides, then close in place.
Lift the isolated egg vertically with closed jaws and verify visible retention.
Egg visibly retained and three remain in basket. Carry above the holder's rear-right cup, keeping the gripper closed and clear of the rim.
Align the retained egg over the rear-right cup and lower toward its bottom, compensating for its slight offset in the jaws.
Descent appears obstructed by the upright lid. Back the held egg toward the front row with a small lift, then reassess clearance.
Replan with a smaller first increment after the rejected action, then retreat from lid contact while retaining the egg.
Lower the visibly retained egg into the front-right cup, now clear of the upright lid.
Release the egg aligned over the front-right cup, then lift away to check that it settles in the holder.

Descend toward the leftmost remaining egg, using a slightly reduced opening to avoid the basket rim.
Refine centering on the left egg and lower the finger contact region before closing in place.
Lift straight upward with closed jaws to verify the second egg is retained.
Egg remained in basket. Reopen and shift the jaw contact region toward the robot and slightly right while descending for a better-centered grasp.
Use the wrist image to shift the contact region slightly left and back toward the egg center, then close without lifting.
Lift vertically while keeping closed and inspect whether this centered grasp retains the egg.
Egg remains in basket. Restore a vertical approach above the isolated left egg to avoid shallow fingertip contact.
Advance the vertical gripper over the left egg and lower with fully open jaws, correcting the wrist-view forward offset.
Small inward and downward adjustment to clear the basket rim, then close around the centered egg and pause.
The closing region passed behind the egg. Reopen and shift toward the robot while holding height to recenter it in the wrist view.
Close on the recentered egg while stationary, then make a short vertical retention lift.

The egg slipped back into the basket. Reapproach the leftmost egg vertically, with a staged alignment before closing.
Descend in a staged approach while bringing the left egg toward the middle of the wrist view; keep jaws open.
Make a smaller final approach to bring the egg equator into the jaw contact region before closing.

Make a controlled lift with closed jaws to check whether the egg stays with the gripper.
Reopen and align to the egg now isolated at the rear of the basket, then reassess jaw alignment.
Center the rear egg slightly right and forward between the jaw pads, then close while stationary.
Lift the rear egg vertically while keeping closed and verify that it clears the basket.
Reopen and approach farther forward so the jaws contact the egg's equator instead of its near end; inspect before closing.

Make a slow short lift with the gripper closed to verify this grasp before transporting.
Egg is retained after the slow lift. Carry it clear of the basket toward the empty front-left cup, with jaws closed.

Lower the open gripper slowly around the isolated egg, avoiding the rim and checking the jaw contact region.

Center the egg at the jaw pads with a small right/back/down adjustment, then close fully while stationary.
Shift inward from the basket wall and close around the isolated egg, keeping height nearly fixed to avoid rim contact.
Retreat from persistent basket-wall contact and change the jaw direction for a clearer approach.

Lift slowly straight up with closed jaws to verify the diagonal grasp retains the egg.

Hold the retained egg stationary in the right gripper while approaching the holder's left lid edge with the left arm.
Bring the left gripper over the lid's left-front edge while the right arm holds its egg clear of the basket.

Try lifting the pinched left edge of the lid along an upward/backward arc; inspect whether the lid follows.

Withdraw left gripper from the lid top and rotate for a side-on pinch of the lid edge, avoiding further downward contact.

Continue rotating the left gripper toward a horizontal side pinch, staying left of the holder and away from the right arm.
Finish orienting the left jaws vertically for a horizontal side pinch, lowering beside the closed lid while keeping its edge clear.
